Among the many Apple Intelligence features coming with iOS 27, the Passwords app is getting a particularly powerful new capability: automatically changing your passwords for you.

The Passwords app in iOS 27, powered by Apple Intelligence, can fix your leaked login credentials on your behalf

The next generation of Apple Intelligence is at the core of the upcoming iOS 27 and related software updates. One powerful new AI feature is closely tied to the Apple Passwords app.

Launched two years ago, the Passwords app is a centralized hub specifically for managing login credentials, two-factor authentication codes, Wi-Fi passwords, passkeys, and more.

The app has always flagged problematic passwords in your vault. For example, if your password has appeared in a data breach or is reused across multiple accounts, the Passwords app will notify you.

But so far, you've always had to manually fix these problematic login credentials yourself.

However, with iOS 27, Apple says its new agentic AI capabilities can change your passwords for you in many situations. According to their website:

With this functionality, you can ensure your credentials are always secure and use strong passwords, while minimizing the time and hassle required.

iOS 27 is currently in beta and will be rolling out to all users in the coming weeks. The new password feature is expected to debut in iOS 27.0, but since the rollout in the beta has been unstable, it may ultimately arrive in iOS 27.1 instead.

Have you tried the new password feature in the iOS 27 beta? How was your experience? Feel free to share in the comments.
